newsitem.title: USA: FPL Group remedies orimulsion deficiencies.
newsitem.headline: FPL Group remedies orimulsion deficiencies.

text.p: Florida Power & Light Co said Tuesday the utility believes it has remedied the deficiencies in its proposed orimulsion project.

The FPL Group Inc subsidiary said it has spent a year improving and refining the project following its rejection by Gov. Lawton Chiles and the Cabinet -- sitting as the Power Plant Siting Board -- in a 4-3 vote in April 1996.
The board, overriding the recommendations of nine agencies and a state hearing officer, cited what it believed were three major community concerns as reasons for denial.
While appealing to the courts, FPL said, it renewed efforts to hear local public concerns and evaluate the issues.
"When FPL began this process in 1994, we placed enormous emphasis on meeting the technical environmental standards required under the Power Plant Siting Act.

"We did not focus enough on the special environmental and public concerns of Manatee County and the Tampa Bay region. We think we have now remedied this deficiency," said C.O. Woody, the utility's senior vice president - power generation.
"Today we have a better project and we have committed to a major environmental enhancement program," Woody said.
The utility wants to use four million metric tonnes of orimulsion a year at its Mantee, Fla., power plant -- a 228 megawatt plant that now burns residual fuel oil.

The orimulsion -- a mixture of water and hydrocarbons from Venezuela's Orinoco Tar Belt -- would come from a $320 million processing plant planned by DuPont Co's Conoco, Norway's Statoil and Venezuela's Bitumenes de Orinoco. The Conoco group plans to start work of the five million tonne per year plant later this year.
Florida Power & Light said it has addressed the three major areas of concern as follows:

-- Nitrogen oxide emissions - There will be no increase in these emissions. FPL will hold total annual nitrogen oxide emissions from the plant to historic levels while reducing the rate of emissions by nearly one half. Overall annual air emissions from the plant will be reduced by 18 percent.

-- Spill prevention, containment and cleanup - FPL will provide up to $1 million toward the cost of installing a vessel tracking system in Tampa Bay. The fuel supplier also confirmed the ability to contain and recover Orimulsion with conventional oil spill recovery equipment during an open water spill demonstration conducted off the coast of Venezuela.
-- Transportation of byproducts - FPL will use rail, instead of trucks, as the primary method of delivering limestone and removing byproducts from the plant.
Separately, FPL said it will commit a portion of the project's fuel savings to establish a 20-year, $200 million trust for environmental enhancement of Tampa Bay.
FPL said it will deposit the first $10 million to the trust within 12 months of commercial operation of Manatee plant using orimulsion.
